summary.text: isTimestamp is a TypeScript type predicate from unknown to string. Its single returned conjunction first requires a string, then a UTC-shaped YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss value with optional fractional seconds and a trailing Z, and finally a finite Date.parse result. Because the checks use &&, a failed earlier check returns false and short-circuits later checks; true requires all three. async function start(): Promise<void> {
  await consumer.connect()
  await consumer.subscribe({ topics: ['weather.place-requested', 'weather.forecast-updated'], fromBeginning: true })
  await consumer.run({ autoCommit: false, eachMessage: consumeMessage })
  consumerReady = true
  app.get('/api/weather', getWeather)
  app.post('/api/places', savePlace)
  app.post<{ Params: { id: string } }>('/api/places/:id/refresh', requestRefresh)
  app.get('/health', getHealth)
  app.get('/openapi.json', getOpenApi)
  app.get('/', getHome)
  await app.listen({ port: Number(process.env.PORT ?? 8080), host: '0.0.0.0' })
}
